fix_commit.message: Limit the NEAR span in FTS3 to 1 billion, to avoid integer overflow. [bugs:/forumpost/4cfcf164d2|Bug report 4cfcf164d2].
fix_commit.author: drh

findings.title: Unbounded NEAR span value leads to signed integer overflow in FTS3 arithmetic
findings.message: In getNextNode() (ext/fts3/fts3_expr.c), the NEAR/N distance parameter from a user-supplied FTS3 query is parsed via sqlite3Fts3ReadInt(), which accepts any value up to INT_MAX (2147483647). No upper bound is enforced on the resulting nNear value before it is stored in pRet->nNear. Later, in fts3EvalNearTrim() (ext/fts3/fts3.c), this value is used in signed integer arithmetic: `int nParam1 = nNear + pPhrase->nToken;` and `int nParam2 = nNear + *pnToken;`. When nNear is near INT_MAX, adding even a small positive token count causes signed integer overflow — undefined behavior in C. This can result in negative nParam values being passed downstream, corrupting position list filtering logic and potentially crashing the process or producing incorrect query results.
findings.suggestion: After parsing nNear with sqlite3Fts3ReadInt(), clamp the value to a safe upper bound (e.g., 1,000,000,000) so that subsequent arithmetic operations such as `nNear + pPhrase->nToken` cannot overflow a 32-bit signed integer.

ground_truth.root_cause: The introducing commit (fc7f31742d) replaced a manual digit-parsing loop with sqlite3Fts3ReadInt(), which correctly prevents overflow during digit accumulation but returns any value from 0 to INT_MAX. No downstream cap was applied before nNear was stored and later used in arithmetic expressions (nNear + pPhrase->nToken), allowing an attacker-controlled large N to trigger signed integer overflow in fts3EvalNearTrim().
